subject: Post-call: Eval scope & acceptance criteria for Orbital Health pilot
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Bethany Sanders <bethany.sanders@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Eval scope & acceptance criteria for Orbital Health pilot

Thanks again for taking the call today — good to meet you, Bethany. Quick recap below and a proposed next-steps plan so we can kick off the pilot evaluation on Redwood.

Recap (30-min call)
- Goal: validate model fit for structured clinical-extraction (discrete fields) and short-form summarization of clinical notes.
- Data: you can provide de-identified CSVs; we'll confirm PII/PHI handling and private deployment options.
- Success criteria: see proposed acceptance thresholds below; we'll measure both automated metrics and a small manual review.

Recommended models to try (first-pass, tuned for latency/cost)
1) redwood-7b-v1-q4f16 — good balance of throughput + extraction accuracy
2) llama2-13b-chat-8bit — higher quality on summarization prompts, higher cost
3) redwood-2b-quant-fast — low-cost baseline for throughput stress tests

Suggested evaluation plan
- Dry run: 200 de-identified rows (sanity checks, format validation) — target 3 business days to validate pipeline.
- Full run: ~500 labeled rows (mix of extraction + summarization) for primary scoring.
- For extraction tasks: provide gold CSV with columns: id, context, prompt, expected_answers (JSON string), metadata_tag.
- For summarization: id, context, prompt, expected_summary.

Scoring & acceptance (proposed)
- Extraction: Exact Match on key fields >= 88% OR F1 (micro) >= 90% across required fields.
- Summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.55 and human pass-rate >= 80% on a 50-sample QA spotcheck.
- Regression guardrail: any model with >5% drop vs baseline on extraction EM will trigger review.

Artifacts we will provide / need
- Redwood will share: evaluation runbook (attached), scoring scripts (python + docker), and a sample prompt bank.
- You provide: 200-row de-identified CSV for dry run (CSV template attached: orbital_sample_prompts.csv).
- Attachments referenced: orbital_sample_prompts.csv, redwood_eval_runbook.pdf

Options for running the eval
- Hosted (recommended for fastest turnaround): data pushed to Redwood staging via secure upload; runs on dedicated sandbox instance.
- Private (recommended if PHI concerns): Redwood Private deployed in your VPC / on-prem; we can run the same eval flow there.

Next steps
1) Confirm whether you will share a de-identified sample (200 rows) by EOD Friday (19 Mar).
2) Tell us if you require Private deployment (we'll route to security).
3) Confirm availability for a 30-min kickoff next week (propose Wed 10–11am PT).

Attachments: orbital_sample_prompts.csv, redwood_eval_runbook.pdf

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben/Marissa as they’ll own the pilot run and security intake.

—
Karthik Iyer
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Bethany Sanders <bethany.sanders@orbitalhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Eval scope & acceptance criteria for Orbital Health pilot

Thanks Karthik — this looks straightforward and helpful. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) PHI / compliance: our data contains PHI. We can prepare a de-identified extract for the dry run, but for the full run we will likely want Redwood to run in our VPC (or provide SOC2/HIPAA assurances). Can you confirm what the security intake looks like and whether you have an on-prem option?

2) Sample size: is 500 rows the minimum you recommend? For some of our rare-extraction labels we don't have that many gold examples — what is your minimum viable size to get meaningful signals?

3) Cost / SLA: can you share a ballpark estimate for the dry run vs full run (compute + engineer time)? Also FYI we need the run to be completed within 10 business days of sending the full dataset.

We can share a 200-row de-identified CSV by Friday. Confirming availability for Wed next week 10am PT should work for our DS lead.

—
Bethany Sanders
Director, Data Science | Orbital Health
bethany.sanders@orbitalhealth.com

Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Eval scope & acceptance criteria for Orbital Health pilot

Hi Bethany — appreciate the quick reply. Short answers: 

- Private / compliance: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC. We also have a SOC 2 Type II report and a HIPAA addendum available; I’m attaching the eval runbook and will open a security intake ticket if you confirm Private is required.
- Minimum sample size: 500 is our recommended minimum for statistically meaningful extraction metrics, but we can run phased analysis — start with 200 de-identified rows for pipeline validation, then incrementally increase. For very rare labels we recommend targeted augmentation or active sampling.
- Cost: Dry run (200 rows) typically covered under our pilot program (no compute charge), full run pricing depends on model family + run size — rough ballpark $2k–$6k for a 500-row run using mid-sized models; procurement team can give formal quote.

On the SLA: we can commit to a 10-business-day turnaround for the full run if we have dataset + access/approvals upfront.

I’m looping in Marissa for security Procurement + deployment orchestration. If Private is confirmed, Marissa will send the security checklist and next steps.

Attachment: redwood_eval_runbook.pdf

Hi Bethany — great to meet you (virtually). I'm Marissa (technical program manager for pilots). Quick operational acceptance criteria and timeline so the procurement/security teams have what they need.

Operational checklist (please confirm):
- Security: we can run in your VPC (Redwood Private) OR run in our hosted sandbox if data is fully de-identified and your legal signs our DPA + HIPAA addendum.
- Contact for security intake: please share your security POC (name + email); we will open the intake and send over the SOC2 docs and an HLD for the Private deployment.

Data / format requirements (required for both dry + full run)
- CSV template for extraction tasks: columns -> id, patient_age, visit_date, context_text, prompt, expected_answers_json, label_source, sample_weight
- For summarization: id, context_text, prompt, expected_summary, summary_length_target
- File encoding: UTF-8, max row size 64k chars; compress with gzip if >50MB.
- Split guidance: dry run (single file, 200 rows), full run (train/val/test split is optional — we require a gold test set of minimum 500 rows).

Scoring rubric (we will run automated + manual QA):
- Extraction (structured fields): Exact Match (per-field) and F1 aggregated across target fields. Passing threshold: EM >= 88% OR micro-F1 >= 90%. Regression alert if any field drops >5% vs baseline.
- Summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.55 AND human QA pass-rate >= 80% on a 50-sample set. If automated metrics are borderline, we escalate to 2-annotator adjudication.
- Edge-cases: for multi-value extraction fields, we will use set-F1; please provide canonicalization rules in metadata column.

Deliverables from Redwood
- Dry-run report (3 business days): format validation, tokenization issues, initial per-field metrics.
- Full-run report (10 business days after dataset sign-off): per-model scoring, per-field error analysis, prompt bank with recommended prompt variants, and top failure cases.

Timeline (proposed)
- Fri 19 Mar: we receive 200-row de-id sample (you confirmed).
- Mon 22 Mar: kickoff call + security intake (if Private required).
- Tue 23 Mar–Thu 25 Mar: dry run and report delivered by Mon 29 Mar.
- Full run (if authorized): 10 business days after dataset + approvals.

If this aligns with your expectations, please: (1) confirm security POC, (2) upload the 200-row sample to the Drive link we shared, or reply with an alternative transfer method, and (3) confirm kickoff slot Wed 10am PT.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive (upload folder)
